This group yields nothing. Its items and categories are empty, or a mod it needs is not loaded
This pool needs a mod that is not loaded, so it has no contents
This is a template. Pools that inherit from it have the contents
The chance for coins to drop from zombies.
The maximum amount of cents that can drop from a zombie.
The minimum amount of cents that can drop from a zombie.
The chance for coins to drop from sprinters.
The maximum amount of cents that can drop from a sprinter.
The minimum amount of cents that can drop from a sprinter.
Blacklist %1 globally? It will stop appearing in every shop on the server from their next restock.
Blacklist %1 items globally? They will stop appearing in every shop on the server from their next restock.
Delete "%1"? This removes your override and cannot be undone.
Clear the following, for every player, permanently? %1
Reset %1's wallet? Their change and unbound balances are cleared. Bound balances stay, since those are the part a reset is meant to preserve.
Force restock ALL shops? This rebuilds every shop's inventory immediately.
"%1" ships with PhunMart, so it can't be deleted, because the built-in version would just come back. Disable it instead?
"%1" ships with PhunMart and can't be deleted. Edit it instead, or point things at a different price.
Everything priced from currency_base follows this. Shops quote the old money until they restock.
Prices were written in cents, so they need scaling down. Watch the table and pick a number that reads well
Anything stackable works. Money is the usual choice because players loot it
Change is deducted from the wallet. An item is taken from the player's bags
What to call this money on screen. Leave blank to use the item name

Named tests a player must pass before an offer can be bought. Attach them from a pool, group, special or item override; every condition on a row must pass. The perk_ entries are generated for the XP shop.
Items barred from every shop. Applies when a machine next restocks. Pool-specific blacklists live on the pool itself, under Pools.
Groups organize items by display category, explicit item lists, or special categories. Referenced by pool sources.

Settings for one specific item, overriding what its group would otherwise decide: what it costs, what it grants, how often it appears. Anything not listed here just uses its group. Marked [off] is disabled.
Every machine standing in the world, nearest first. Double-click a row to teleport to it. Right-clicking a shop on the Shops tab narrows this to that shop.
Recent changes may require one or more shops to restock in order for changes to take effect.

Pools are the shelves a shop restocks from: each gathers groups, and can set a fallback price and stock for items that name neither. Zones limit a pool to certain map difficulties, months to certain times of year. Marked [S] is always available, [off] is disabled.
Named price templates that can be assigned to items. Define cost, currency pool, and amount.
Token reward rules for gameplay actions like zombie kills and playtime. Controls how players earn tokens.
Every shop type and how many machines are standing in the world. Right-click a row for its locations.
Non-item rewards like traits, XP, and boosts. Each special defines an action, display, and optional price/weight.
Everything that isn't editing a definition. Pick a tool to see what it does, then run it.
What every player is holding. Double-click a balance to change it, or right-click a name to pick which one. A bound balance is the part that survives a wallet reset.
Enter a number of 0 or more
Add at least one item, category or special
Enter both a min and a max, or leave both blank
Max must not be less than min
What buying this does to the player
What buying this does. They run in the order listed
These items are asked for in different amounts. Leave blank to keep them, or set one for all of them
Change is in dollars; tokens and items are counted whole. Fill the second box to roll a random price between the two
Optional override for the shop window image, under media/textures/. Empty uses the front of the 3D texture
XP rate multiplier while the boost lasts
Active XP boost level, 0 to 3. Leave a box blank for no bound on that end
How many of each item the player must be carrying
Name for this test. Reusing a name that ships edits that entry rather than making a new one
Which skill the level is read from
Tests a player must pass before this can be bought. All of them must pass
Tests a player must pass, added to whatever the other layers already ask for. All of them must pass
(optional) roll: overrides the shop's items per restock, for this set only
(optional) Default texture for items without one
Whether players can destroy this shop's machines with a sledgehammer. Server default follows the sandbox option. Admins can always destroy them
Name the player sees in the shop
factor: multiplies the inherited amount. Blank = 1

What buying anything in this group gives the player. An item override can change it
What everything in this group costs
Vehicle scripts sold by this group. The buyer gets the one they picked
Anything not set here comes from this entry
inherit: the price this one starts from (optional)
Required. The id other definitions refer to. Cannot be changed later
The id other definitions refer to. Fixed once created
Display name for this group's category in the shop UI
Skill level, 0 to 10. Leave a box blank for no bound on that end
The machine's picture: its 3D model and its shop window. Files live in media/textures/phunmart/
A file in media/textures/phunmart/ by name (e.g. my-machine), or a path under media/textures/
Fails once the player has bought this offer this many times
Passes only while the player holds fewer bound tokens than this
(optional) Min tiles from the nearest shop of this type or category
Only stocked during these in-game months, 1 to 12 (eg 12 for December only). Blank sells all year
Whether players can pick up this shop's machines and place them elsewhere. Server default follows the sandbox option. Admins can always move them
Total minutes played (game time, not real world time). Leave blank to ignore this milestone.
Barred from this pool only. Untick to restore.
(optional) Only used by items whose group sets no price
What buying anything from this pool gives the player. A group or an item override can change it
The groups this pool draws its items from
Select a pool and press Edit to change how often it is drawn from
How often this pool is drawn from, relative to the others in this set. 1 is the usual share, 0.5 is half of it
Tick if this machine only runs on electricity. It shows the unpowered sprites and cannot be opened while the power is off
What it costs. Leave as it is to follow the template
probability: relative chance in the placement lottery. 0 = manual placement only
Starting profession keys, comma separated. The player needs any one of them
(optional) In-game hours before this machine turns into a different shop. Blank follows the sandbox setting, 0 never changes
Per character resets on death. Per account does not
(optional) Offers sharing a name share one allowance, for pick one of these, once
Two shops sharing a category are kept apart in the world. Blank spaces this shop against its own type only
Untick to stop this shop being placed. Machines already standing stay put
The shop type. Fixed once created, since placed machines refer to it
How many items this shop draws each restock. Any pool set below can override it for its own shelf
Optional. Shown instead of the key, unless this shop has a translated name
Perk name as the game spells it, e.g. Cooking or Aiming
Percent condition a bought vehicle arrives in, rolled fresh per part. Blank leaves it as the game spawned it
Percent of the vehicle's own tank it arrives with, so one range suits a truck and a small car. Blank leaves whatever the game put in
(optional) Second image drawn over the icon, e.g. a tier badge
(optional) PNG path under media/, or a script item name, to use as the icon
4 tile sprite names (E, S, W, N facing)
Ignores stock rules: every item always on the shelf, unlimited
What this condition measures. The fields below change to match
Optional. Shown instead of the key in these lists
Which trait to give or take away
Leave blank for unlimited stock. Fill the second box to roll a random amount between the two
4 tile sprite names (E, S, W, N) shown when the machine needs power and has none

Layout mode for the shop UI
weight: relative to others in the same pool. Higher appears more often. Default 1.0
(optional) weight: how often this appears. Higher is more common
In-game hours since the world started. Leave a box blank for no bound on that end

Templates are not sold by anything. Other entries copy them, so editing one changes every entry that copies it. Untick to see them, listed first. Typing a filter finds them anyway.
Show only what you have customised. Blue stripe: you created it. Amber stripe: you edited one that ships with PhunMart.
Click to go to what uses this.
Charge in an item such as money instead of the built-in change, and rescale every price to suit.
Set up a new machine step by step: how it looks, where it spawns, and what it stocks.
Machines already placed keep their old stock until they restock. Lists the ones your edits have affected.
Re-reads the override files from disk. Only needed after editing them by hand; saving in here already does it.
Clear wallets, purchase history and reward tracking for everyone at once. Pick what goes; nothing is ticked to start with.
Rerolls the stock of every machine in the world at once, changing what everyone can currently buy.
No price: these will not appear in a shop unless the pool sets one
Needs four names, one per facing. Found %1
Needs at least one letter or number
That gives the key %1, which is already taken
2D tiles, shown when a player turns 3D machines off. The generic machine needs no art of its own
The image behind the shop window
Image filename from your own mod
Two shops sharing a category are kept apart in the world
Tiles from the nearest shop of this type or category. Blank follows the sandbox setting (%1)
Shown to players. The key is taken from this
Fallback price, used when an item has none of its own
Chance of appearing relative to other shops, most of which use 15. Higher is more common, 0 is manual placement only
Hours between restocks. Blank follows the sandbox setting (%1)
Fewest and most it offers after a restock. It picks somewhere in this range each time
Four tile names from your tileset, comma separated: east, south, west, north
The machine's picture: its 3D model and its shop window. Pick one to look like that shop
What does the machine look like?
How much does it stock, and at what price?
Balance of %1 will be restored on death.
Your wallet balance across all currency pools
If enabled, players can drop currency from their wallet as a pickupable item. Intentional drops are always pickupable by any player, regardless of the wallet pickup setting.
The chance that a vanilla vending machine will get converted to a random PhunMart machine. Set to 0 to disable
Chance for zombies to drop coins
The probability that a zombie will drop coins upon death.
Maximum cents a player can carry (9999 = $99.99). At cap, coins left on the ground will not be consumed. Set to 0 for no cap.

How a zombie's coin drop reaches the player. This only picks the form it arrives in: the drop chance and the min/max amounts above still apply to all three, as does any per-zone tuning from PhunZones.
Adds more verbose logging for debugging purposes. Only use if you know what you're doing.
The minimum distance between similarly grouped machines
The default number of hours between restocking a shop. 0 would mean that (by default) the shops are only ever stocked once

How many hours before a machine becomes a different shop entirely, picked from the ones eligible where it stands. 0 means machines keep the shop they converted as. A machine waits until no player is nearby before changing.
Default number of items to stock
How many items a shop stocks when it does not set a roll count of its own. This is the low end of a small range, so 5 stocks 5 to 8. Most shops set their own count and ignore this.
If set, only players whose role name matches this value (case-insensitive) can open the editor. Leave empty to allow all players with access to debug/admin menu (or always allow in singleplayer).
Show the change (coin) currency pool in the shop UI and wallet tab. Disabling hides it from players but does not delete balances.
Show the token currency pool in the shop UI and wallet tab. Disabling hides it from players but does not delete balances.
The maximum number of cents a zombie can drop upon death.
Maximum number of items allowed in a sticky pool before a warning is logged. Sticky pools always show all their items in a shop. Keep this low to avoid cluttered shops.
The minimum number of cents a zombie can drop upon death.
If enabled, players can destroy shop machines with a sledgehammer. A shop can override this in its Basics tab. Admins can always destroy machines.
If enabled, players can pick up and move shop machines like any other furniture. A shop can override this in its Basics tab. Admins can always move machines.
Maximum number of special tokens a player can carry. Set to 0 for no cap.
What happens to a balance on death

Dropped leaves a wallet on the ground where the player died, to be walked back for, scaled by the return rate below. It lands on the ground rather than on the corpse so that a zombie wandering into a zone that clears zombies cannot carry it off. Kept moves the balance straight to the next character, with nothing to recover. Lost wipes it. Bound pools such as tokens are restored to their allowance in all three.
If enabled, only the owner of a wallet can pick it up.

The percentage of money that is returned to the player on death. 0 means no money is returned, 100 means all money is returned. Only applies when a balance is dropped on the body; the other two options have nothing to scale.
